title: Terminar por and Acabar por: Ending Up

sections.content:
*Terminar por* + infinitive and *acabar por* + infinitive mean the same thing: "to end up doing something" or "to finally do it". They describe the last step of a process, often after doubts, delays or resistance, and the result is often not what was planned. You know *acabar de* from A2 Unit 32, but *acabar por* is a different phrase, so watch the last word: *de* looks back at something just done, *por* points to where a process finally arrives.

Both verbs can be conjugated in any tense (*terminó por aceptar*, *acabaremos por entender*). After *por* the verb is always an infinitive.

sections.title: terminar por / acabar por + infinitive
rows: Después de dudar mucho, terminó por aceptar el trabajo.
After doubting a lot, she ended up accepting the job.
El mayordomo acabó por dejarlo quedarse.
The manager finally let him stay.
Si sigues así, acabarás por cansarte.
If you go on like this, you will end up getting tired.
No terminó por entender la explicación.
He never did come to understand the explanation.

sections.content: Use these phrases when there is a process behind the result. For a simple event with no story before it, use the plain verb: say *Compró el coche*, not *Terminó por comprar el coche*, unless something happened first, such as a long search.
